input: Every checkout attempt has returned a 502 for the last eleven minutes.
Search returns results but takes eleven seconds on every query.
Export puts commas inside unquoted address fields and the file breaks in Excel.
The settings icon sits two pixels off centre in the account menu.
Report generation fails for any date range longer than a month.
The date picker will not accept the last day of February in a leap year.
A tooltip says Sign In where the button underneath says Log in.
The public API is answering 503 to every caller and has been since 04:12.
Pagination shows page three of two when a filter removes the final page.
The empty-state illustration is stretched on very wide monitors.
Customers open the dashboard and their entire project list is empty.
The mobile app crashes on launch for users on Android 13.
Our footer still shows last year.
Card captures are all failing at the processor with an authentication error.
Notification mail has been arriving roughly forty minutes late since noon.
Sorting by owner puts lowercase names after every uppercase one.
Our primary database failed over and the replica refuses every write.
Bulk import accepts the file and then fails at ninety percent, every time.
The help link in the sidebar points at last year's documentation.
The spinner keeps turning for a moment after the content has arrived.
Two of our five API nodes are unhealthy and requests are timing out.
Times on the activity feed are UTC while the rest of the product is local.
Dark mode leaves one divider at the light-mode colour.
The whole EU region has been unreachable from the internet for twenty minutes.
Deleting a saved view leaves it in the recently-used list.
Counts read as one items when a list holds exactly one entry.
Nobody in any tenant can obtain a session; sign-in is down.
The admin console will not load for anyone with more than five hundred users.
The success message disappears faster than most people can read it.
A production migration dropped the audit table instead of the staging copy.
Attachments upload but cannot be downloaded again from the ticket view.
The API accepts a negative quantity on a line item without complaining.
Session cookies issued this morning resolve to the wrong customer account.
Charts render, but the numbers are a day behind the data underneath them.
Keyboard shortcuts stop responding after the command palette is closed.
Column widths reset when the table re-renders after a filter change.
Single sign-on works for Okta tenants and fails for everyone on Azure AD.
Two people submitting the form at once can create duplicate tags.
The billing subdomain still serves the old logo as its site icon.
Enrolment codes for two-factor are being delivered to a stranger's phone.
Filters reset whenever the browser tab regains focus.
The billing page has lost the hover state on its secondary buttons.
Webhook delivery stopped entirely and the queue is four hundred thousand events deep.
The scheduler runs hourly jobs twice, though the second run does nothing.
A dialog offers Cancel for both the safe choice and the destructive one.
Nightly backups have written zero bytes for six days and nobody noticed.
Autocomplete has stopped suggesting anything for non-Latin scripts.
Long project names overflow the breadcrumb instead of being truncated.
The billing job double-charged every subscription that renewed on Tuesday.
Our content delivery network is serving stale assets to about a fifth of visitors.
Our published payload documentation describes a field we removed in March.
The onboarding checklist ticks a step before that step has been done.
Retries have backed off to six hours and partners are complaining about it.
Percentages in the summary round to a hundred while the rows sum to ninety-nine.
Screen readers announce the sort control as a button with no name.
Uploads above two megabytes are silently truncated and the stored file is corrupt.
A retried request creates a second comment when the first one had succeeded.
Focus jumps from the search box straight to the footer on the reports page.
Our TLS certificate expired at midnight and browsers now refuse the site.
A malformed cursor gets a 200 with a truncated page instead of an error.
Our brand blue fails contrast against white at small sizes.
Indexing wrote one tenant's customer records into another tenant's index.
The billing run generates invoices correctly and attaches no PDF.
Concurrent edits to a description keep whichever save landed last, silently.
The rate limiter is treating all authenticated traffic as anonymous and blocking it.
Throughput halved after the last deploy and no error rate moved at all.
The permission check runs after the query, so a refusal still logs a read.
Printing drops the table header from every page after the first.
A tenant with a custom domain gets signed out every twelve minutes.
Bulk actions apply to the filtered set or the selected set depending on click order.
Transitions animate even when the reduce-motion preference is set.
Reset links sent in the past hour grant access without the token being checked.
Limit headers report the wrong window for an hour after a plan upgrade.
Error text is announced once and removed before it can be read again.
Read replicas drifted eleven hours behind and reporting is quoting stale money.
One integration's retry storm is starving everybody else's queue.
The German translation runs forty percent longer and clips in the navigation.
A deploy rolled back but half the fleet is still serving the new schema.
Metrics show healthy pods while customers see intermittent connection resets.
Archived items keep appearing in search until the next reindex, up to an hour.
Support says three enterprise tenants can see each other's invoices.
Import succeeds and silently skips rows whose currency column is blank.
The changelog feed omits entries published while the cache was warming.
Nobody agrees whether the current wording is wrong or merely unfashionable.
Our audit log stopped recording deletions about three weeks ago.
Two customers describe one symptom and only one of them has the misconfiguration.
The design system says one thing and the shipped component says another.
The export pipeline has been dropping one row in forty since the weekend.
It only happens for accounts created before the schema change in 2023.
It is broken on one designer's monitor and correct on everyone else's.
Our queue consumer acknowledges messages it never actually processed.
Two services disagree about a plan and the interface flickers between them.
A customer called it a defect and product calls it the intended behaviour.
An expired role is stopping every scheduled job from starting at all.
Background sync drains battery on iOS and people are uninstalling over it.
It only takes one click to work around, and nobody can find the click.
Feature flags evaluated default-on and exposed an unreleased pricing page.
It only affects one very large customer, and only during their nightly batch.
Our REST and GraphQL surfaces behave differently and both look deliberate.
The label is accurate and three people in a row misread it the same way.
The behaviour matches the specification and contradicts what we told the customer.
A field is optional in the schema, required in the interface, ignored by the worker.
It only shows at 110 percent browser zoom, which four accounts use.
Latency looks normal but a third of API responses carry an empty body.
The report is right; the expectation came from a sales deck two years old.
Changing it would break a screenshot in a published integration guide.
Only customers on the legacy plan are affected, and they are our largest ten.
Three reports look identical to support and have three different root causes.
The spacing is inconsistent with a page we are about to redesign anyway.
Nothing is down, yet reconciliation shows forty thousand pounds with no order behind it.
It reproduces on staging once in fifty attempts and never in production.
Only Safari on managed devices sees it, and only after a policy sync.
It is intermittent and it disappears whenever we attach a debugger.
A partner's clock is eight minutes fast and our idempotency window rejects them.
Our own internal tenant cannot reproduce it because every flag is on there.
It is cosmetic today and becomes structural after the migration.
The fault is in a dependency we vendored two years ago and no longer patch.
It is trivial to fix and it is not trivial to ship mid-quarter.
Two teams have each filed it against the other team's component.
A vendor changed a default and our webhook signatures no longer verify.
